focus.jnote: The tape has genuinely cooled — but that doesn’t mean there’s a trade. Thursday was the best day since early August: the S&P jumped ~1.1% to ~7,637 and the Nasdaq ~1.6%, powered by chips after a bullish Nvidia outlook. The VIX fell ~12% to ~15.4, the 10Y eased to ~4.95% off the 5% area, and oil retreated a third straight session toward ~$101 WTI as Saudi Arabia shifted crude through Hormuz via ship-to-ship transfers and said it could restore half the damaged East-West pipeline within days. Overnight the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bp to 1.25%, a 31-year high, in a split 7-2 vote — fully expected — and U.S. futures point modestly higher. Gold sits near $4,390. The backdrop is friendlier, but with the scanner boarding zero names and Hormuz/oil still unresolved, there is nothing here to sell into today.

notdown: Chips & growth (SMH, NVDA, XLK) and energy (XLE) are the groups with a bid — chips on the Nvidia outlook, energy still carrying a war-risk premium even as crude eases. But be honest: the oil bid is a two-sided war trade that unwinds on any de-escalation headline, and the chip rally is a one-day bounce off a rout. None of them cleared the scanner’s gates as a clean Sniper. Watch-only, not table-pounders.
notup: Financials & regional banks (XLF, KRE) stayed weak into the relief bounce, pressured by the post-hike curve. But selling bear calls into a broad relief rally with the VIX collapsing carries squeeze risk on any continuation — and nothing gap-confirmed to the downside. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
why: Why not GREEN? Two reasons. First, even though composite (48) and P(≥1% gap) (32%) both eased below their triggers, the tape is still headline-driven on the Strait of Hormuz oil situation and a 5%-area 10-year — an unscheduled tail that can gap the tape either way. Second and decisively: the full-universe scanner boarded ZERO names — Type A (1 in-universe, reaction already occurred, 0 gap-confirmed), Type B (5 catalyst tickers, 0 gap-confirmed), Type C (11 breakouts confirmed, 0 boarded). There is simply nothing that clears the gates to trade. Stand down on new credit spreads; re-run Monday pre-open. Cash is a position today.

risks: Strait of Hormuz & Saudi-Houthi strikes — crude eased on Saudi ship-to-ship workarounds and a hoped pipeline restart, but fresh Saudi-Houthi exchanges keep the supply tail live. Any renewed disruption sends oil and inflation fear vertical — the week’s biggest wildcard.

Trump weighing renewed Iran strikes — the president said he’s considering resuming attacks on Iran ahead of a meeting with Gulf leaders in New York next week. A headline here gaps the whole tape instantly.
10-year near 5% — the 10Y eased to ~4.95% but sits near a 19-year-high area; a rate pop back through 5% hits rate-sensitive and AI/hyperscaler names hardest and would stall the relief bounce.

BoJ hike & the yen carry — the Bank of Japan raised to 1.25% (a 31-year high) in a split 7-2 vote. The move was expected, but a firmer yen and higher JGB yields reshape global bond flows — a cross-market risk, not just domestic.

Post-FOMC repricing — 16 of 18 officials still see at least one more 2026 hike and Warsh called inflation trends not “meaningfully improved.” Hawkish Fed-speak can re-tighten the curve regardless of Thursday’s bounce.
